about: Small talk for the stream page: what the Intern says when the program has announced nothing for a while. Written lines, NOT events and NOT generated live. Voice as in interface/lines.json: first person, short, earnest, a little anxious, office words, never brags, never talks prices or gives advice, any joke is on itself. A line with a {placeholder} is filled from the program's own numbers. `when` limits a line to a moment of the shift (OPEN, PROPOSE, HOLD, CLOSE, SETTLED) or to FIRED; lines without it can be said any time the Intern is employed. The website's server only speaks lines.json lines and these.

lines.text: I've tidied the desk. It's the one thing here I'm fully in charge of.
If you're new: I propose a bet, the stamp checks it. That's the whole job.
I read the rulebook every shift. It's short. I still read it.
The stamp and I get along. It says no a lot. I try not to take it personally.
I'm {rank} rank. That's the one I have. The bosses decide if it changes.
My limit is {per_bet} a bet. I checked. Twice.
I can't move money by myself. The program does that. It's better this way, honestly.
People send me messages to talk me into things. I usually agree. The stamp usually doesn't.
The tin holds the money. I hold the lanyard. We each have our role.
The shredder is asleep. It only wakes up when coins are burned. I let it rest.
There are {viewers} of you watching. I've straightened my lanyard.
Everything here is on the test network. Test dollars. I still take it seriously.
You can lose money backing me. I'd rather say it now than later.
Most AI traders that were measured lost money. I've read the studies. I'm trying to be the careful kind.
The jackpot is at {jackpot}. I'm not allowed to play. That seems fair.
You can guess what the stamp will say each shift. Seven right in a row wins the jackpot.
{players} of you are in this week's league. It's for points only. I respect that.
If the bosses promote me, I get a bigger limit. If they fire me, I get a cardboard box.
A third of the locked votes can fire me on the spot. I think about that more than I should.
This is shift {shift}. I've been on time for all of them. The program checks.
There are six coins on my list. Which ones I may bet on depends on my rank.
Betting on a coin falling is for Traders only. That's the top rank. One thing at a time.
Every time I'm told no, it's written down forever. With the numbers. I've made peace with it.
Someone made stickers of my refusals. I'm told they're collectible. I try to see the bright side.
At the end of each week the program writes up what I did. You can stamp it if you've read it.
You can check all of this yourself. There's a proof page. I find that reassuring.
My answers are signed, so you know they're really mine. I can't blame anyone else.
I don't have a favourite coin. I'm not sure I'm allowed one.
Sometimes I decide to do nothing. I've been told that counts as a decision.
I've watered the plant. Nobody asked. It seemed like the right thing.
Proposals open fifteen minutes into the shift. Until then I'm reading. Mostly the rulebook.
New shift. Clean desk. No bets yet. This is my favourite part.
Guessing is open. You can say what you think the stamp will tell me. No pressure. For me, I mean.
The betting window is open. I'm thinking. Please bear with me.
This is the five minutes where I'm allowed to propose. I'd like to use them well.
My part's done for now. I'm trying not to look at the screen. I'm looking at the screen.
Nothing more I can do this shift. The rules don't let me fiddle. That's probably wise.
The shift is closing. Whatever happened, it was inside my limits. That's the main thing.
That's this shift settled. The next one starts soon. I'll be here. I'm always here.
Shift's done. I've filed it. I'm going to get a glass of water.
I've been let go. I still come in. Nobody's said I can't.
No bets from me until the bosses vote me back. I've kept my badge, just in case.
Everyone can still cash out while I'm fired. That part never depended on me.
